items.title: Duplicate of #7: generate typed mutations around changed optimization guards
items.body:
## Action
Add a bounded, change-directed mode to the existing pass comparison tools. Use a rewrite's regression seed and typed dependency neighborhood to exercise both successful and rejected guard conditions.

## Research basis
**Optimization-Directed Compiler Fuzzing for Continuous Translation Validation** (Optimuzz), Kwon et al., PLDI 2025, sections 3–4: https://prosys.kaist.ac.kr/publications/pldi25.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.1145/3729275 . The paper combines directed generation with translation validation. Its LLVM/TurboFan integrations are not drop-in Starshine implementations.

## Existing work and dependency
Build on #8, `src/validate/gen_valid.mbt`, `src/fuzz`, `scripts/lib/pass-fuzz-compare-task.ts`, and the existing generator profiles, semantic oracle, and reducer. Do not introduce another top-level harness or replace `HotFunc` as the owned IR.

## Possible implementation
1. Accept a selected rule ID, seed fixture, and explicit work budget. Resolve rule IDs through the diagnostic map rather than parsing arbitrary source code.
2. Start with CFG-preserving substitutions in a small def-use neighborhood: same-typed constants, signed/unsigned boundaries, operand aliasing, reused local sources, and alternate producers.
3. Add paired inputs on either side of a rewrite precondition. For effect-sensitive rules, place existing supported effectful producers before and after the candidate without violating typing.
4. Validate every candidate independently. Invalid generation, unsupported features, timeout, no firing, and semantic disagreement must remain different outcomes.
5. Retain candidates using new rule/guard coverage, not merely program size or broad line coverage. Preserve a portion of unguided inputs to avoid one-rule overfitting.
6. Use the existing reducer with a predicate that preserves the selected rule firing and the original mismatch class.

## Acceptance criteria
- Demonstrate a bounded improvement in selected-rule firing versus the current generator using identical seeds, input counts, and time limits.
- Include near-miss controls, unchanged-rule controls, and seeded faulty transformations that the oracle rejects.
- Replay metadata identifies source/binary hashes, rule map, feature policy, input seed, pass options, and observation mode.
- A timeout or unsupported semantic case never counts as verified equivalence.

## Constraints
This is test tooling, not a production optimization. Reuse bounded scratch and enforce mutation/depth/output limits. No always-on telemetry or solver dependency in release builds. Preserve `agent-todo.md` ownership of P00 and performance work; use small focused runs during development and leave long campaigns deferred. Do not create the separate private cross-project research harness.

items.body:
CODEX_READY:true
TASK_MODE:REAL_DELIVERABLES
PRIORITY:P1_INPUT_INTEGRITY

## VERIFIED SOURCE / OWNER CHECK
- Current production source: `Catalog/XmlCatalog.cs` -> `Inspect`, `Preview`, `Document`, `PathOf`.
- `Inspect(xml,itemPath)` currently executes `d.XPathSelectElements(itemPath).ToList()` for a caller-supplied ItemPath. `Preview(xml,source)` executes `Document(xml).XPathSelectElements(source.ItemPath)` directly.
- The source validates mapped field-relative paths with a restrictive regex, but there is no equivalent canonical grammar/preflight for `ItemPath` itself before XPath evaluation.
- Auto-discovery already produces simple absolute element paths through `PathOf`, so the production contract can be constrained to the path shapes the application actually emits rather than accepting arbitrary XPath expressions.
- Open/closed issue search for XmlCatalog ItemPath/XPath validation returned no exact owner; raw PR search for `XmlCatalog ItemPath XPath` returned no PR.
- Existing XML owners for 25 MB document bounds, DTD prohibition, SSRF/fetching, source mapping and XML Variant Mapping are not reopened. XML Variant Mapping remains explicitly out of scope.

## VERIFIED PRODUCTION GAP
A malformed ItemPath can surface XPath parser/evaluation exceptions outside the application's typed validation path. More importantly, arbitrary XPath syntax (descendant selectors, unions, predicates/functions, etc.) can select a much broader or semantically different node set than the simple repeat-node path the XML import UI is designed around. `Inspect` also materializes every match before taking a 20-row sample, making broad/wrong ItemPath expressions unnecessarily expensive even though the source XML itself is bounded.

## REAL PRODUCTION DELIVERABLE
1. Define one canonical product-repeat ItemPath grammar shared by `Inspect` and `Preview`, derived from the existing `PathOf` output and current non-variant XML workflow. At minimum support deterministic absolute element-only paths required by auto-discovery; reject unsupported XPath operators/functions/predicates/unions/descendant tricks with a typed actionable validation error.
2. Compile/validate ItemPath before evaluation. No raw `XPathException`/`ArgumentException` may escape normal Inspect/Preview UI flows for user-configured paths.
3. Preserve current namespace-normalization behavior from `Document`; validation must happen against the normalized local-name document contract rather than inventing namespace mappings.
4. Make Inspect counting/sampling bounded in memory: return the true match count required by the current `XmlScan` contract, but do not materialize all matching `XElement` objects merely to keep the first 20/sample 3 rows. Iterate/count with bounded sample retention or an equivalent allocation-safe strategy.
5. Keep the existing 100,000-product Preview ceiling deterministic. ItemPath validation failure or too-many-items failure occurs before any catalog mutation.
6. Ensure source configuration save/test paths reuse the same canonical validator so a path accepted by Inspect cannot later fail under Preview because of grammar drift.

## REAL PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT
XML source workspace -> source test/inspect -> `XmlCatalog.Inspect` -> saved ItemPath -> `XmlCatalog.Preview` -> catalog import preview/apply.

## ACCEPTANCE / TESTS
- Auto-discovered `/root/products/product`-style path passes Inspect and Preview with identical node selection.
- Empty/whitespace, malformed bracket/quote syntax, union (`|`), arbitrary predicate/function, descendant (`//`) and unsupported axis expressions fail with typed validation messages; no raw XPath parser exception reaches UI.
- A valid path with zero matches reports the existing explicit no-record condition.
- 100,000 matching products remain supported under the existing Preview limit; 100,001 fails deterministically before catalog mutation.
- Inspect over a large bounded document reports the exact match count while retaining only bounded sample/path-discovery state, not a list of every match.
- Namespace-bearing source remains compatible with the current local-name normalization behavior.
- ItemPath accepted during source validation remains accepted after restart and by Preview.
- Malformed field-relative mapping paths continue to be rejected under their existing separate rules.

## EDGE CASES
- Unicode XML element names permitted by the application's actual normalized-name contract
- root-only path and deeply nested but bounded paths
- duplicate local names at different depths
- namespace prefixes removed during normalization
- zero matches, exactly 100k, 100001
- invalid XPath tokens that previously threw from `XPathSelectElements`
- source settings edited after Inspect but before Preview

- Preserve `DtdProcessing.Prohibit`, `XmlResolver=null`, 25 MB document bound and all existing remote-fetch protections.
- No secret/token/PAT/password/API key/PII or raw supplier payload is logged in validation diagnostics.

items.title: Duplicate of #7: measure rewrite-rule coverage in pass-local comparisons
items.body:
## Action
Extend the existing pass-local comparison lane with coverage of individual rewrite decisions. A successful run must distinguish a pass that was invoked from a rewrite that actually changed the input.

This is a proposed testing improvement, not a report of a confirmed compiler defect.

## Research basis
Kwon et al., **Optimization-Directed Compiler Fuzzing for Continuous Translation Validation**, PLDI 2025, sections 3–4. The transferable idea is to aim testing at specific optimization conditions instead of relying on whole-compiler coverage.
- Paper: https://prosys.kaist.ac.kr/publications/pldi25.pdf
- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1145/3729275

## Existing implementation and scope
Reuse `src/passes`, `src/cmd/optimizer_reports.mbt`, `scripts/lib/pass-fuzz-compare-task.ts`, and `scripts/lib/fuzz-summary-counters.ts`. `docs/wiki/tooling/pass-fuzz-compare.md` already describes pass admission, minimum comparison counts, semantic execution, and reduction. Do not rebuild those features. Check existing counters first and add only missing rule-level information.

## Possible implementation
1. Give a small initial set of OptimizeInstructions and DAE2 rewrite sites stable diagnostic IDs. Keep the ID mapping separate from source line numbers.
2. Record bounded counts for candidate visited, guard rejected, rewrite committed, and later invalidated/rolled back where applicable. Count a rewrite only after the mutation succeeds.
3. Include pass options, input hash, source revision, rule-map version, and actual firing counts in existing comparison artifacts.
4. Add an opt-in requirement that selected rules fire at least a configured number of times. Reject unknown rule IDs. A zero-fire lane must be reported as insufficient coverage, not successful qualification.
5. Keep aggregate reporting separate from semantic results. Rule firing does not establish correctness or profitability.

## Tests and acceptance criteria
- A small fixture fires each initial rule; a near-miss fixture reaches the guard but does not fire it.
- A disabled rule and a no-op pass fail the required-fire gate.
- Output bytes and observable behavior agree with ordinary builds when diagnostics are disabled.
- Compare original and transformed programs through the existing semantic lane; retain trap and effect-order observations.

labels.name: windows-os

items.body:
Correction after retesting: **Maximize/Restore works in Moonlight touch mode. Only Minimize and Close fail.** Closing as a duplicate of #47289 at the reporter’s request.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.930.31730 (build 12947, prod), confirmed through the desktop app's version/update-check tool.
Microsoft Store package version: OpenAI.Codex 26.930.3930.0.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided. This report concerns desktop window input behavior.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows, Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.22631.0, x64.
Accessing the Windows desktop through Moonlight streaming with touch mode enabled.
Moonlight client platform/version and streaming host software/version have not been collected.

### What issue are you seeing?

In the Codex Windows desktop app, Moonlight touch mode cannot activate the top-right Minimize and Close (X) controls. Maximize / Restore works in touch mode after retesting.

This is localized to those three buttons among the controls tested. Touch input works on the top-left File, Edit, View, and Help menus, the back-navigation control, split-pane controls, and the chat/content area. The app remains responsive. Other controls have not been exhaustively tested.

Switching the same streaming session to Moonlight mouse mode makes all three top-right buttons work normally.

| Control | Moonlight touch mode | Moonlight mouse mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimize | No window action | Works |
| Maximize / Restore | Works | Works |
| Close | No window action | Works |

These input results were confirmed by the user during troubleshooting; they were not reproduced through automated touch injection.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Stream a Windows desktop running Codex through Moonlight.
2. Enable Moonlight touch mode.
3. Open Codex and tap each of the three top-right window controls.
4. Observe that Minimize and Close do not perform their window actions, while Maximize/Restore works.
5. Tap the top-left menus, back-navigation control, or split-pane controls and observe that touch interaction works.
6. Switch Moonlight to mouse mode.
7. Click the same three top-right window controls and observe that all work normally.

### What is the expected behavior?

Touch-mode input delivered through Moonlight should activate the three window controls, just as mouse-mode input does, while retaining normal touch interaction elsewhere in the app.

### Additional information

Duplicate of #47289. After retesting, the reporter confirmed the same affected controls: Minimize and Close fail with touch, while Maximize/Restore works. This observation was made through Moonlight streaming.

Read-only inspection of the installed app bundle found Windows window configuration using `titleBarStyle: "hidden"` and `titleBarOverlay`. This is a diagnostic clue, not proof of a root cause. It is not yet established whether the failure originates in Codex/Electron's window controls, the streaming input translation, or their interaction.

Current workaround: use Moonlight mouse mode for these three controls. No application files or system input settings were changed during investigation.

Hi,

We started seeing this after last week's update. With CSS Print Method set to Internal Embedding, saving an Elementor page returns the page's CSS in front of the JSON response.

The save itself works. Changes are stored and a new revision is created. But the admin-ajax.php response for save_builder starts like this:

{"success":true,"data":{"responses":{"save_builder":{"success":true,"code":200, ...

items.title: Duplicate of #109: anonymous organization base-table hardening
items.body:
Follow-up discovered during Issue #108 security-advisor classification.

## Finding
Anonymous RLS on active `organizations` / `organization_locations` plus default table grants allows direct anonymous SELECT of all base-table columns, including internal metadata such as `created_by`. Public discovery already has curated SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (`public_partner_directory`, `public_partner_profile`, `public_partner_profile_details`, `public_active_offers`) and current frontend code does not rely on anonymous direct table reads.

## Goal
Make the curated public RPCs the anonymous public-read boundary while preserving authenticated organization/editor behavior.

## Scope
- revoke anonymous SELECT on `public.organizations` and `public.organization_locations`;
- do not revoke authenticated reads;
- preserve anonymous EXECUTE on the four intentional public RPCs;
- add pgTAP/security regression proving anon cannot direct-select the two base tables but can still call the curated public RPCs;
- no schema/data deletion, no RLS weakening, no production DNS/provider changes.

## Acceptance
1. `anon` cannot SELECT base organization/location tables.
2. `authenticated` remains able to use existing organization/profile/editor flows under RLS.
3. Four curated public RPCs remain executable by anon and return only their declared public projection.
4. Database QA and normal repo gates are green.
5. Issue #108 records this as remediated rather than merely classified.
